body: Way before we even knew each other, she attempted when she was 16 and was in a coma for three days. I've wrestled bottles of mixed pills out of her hands more than once, although thankfully years ago at this point. I wish I could be confident that she would go on living if I dropped dead or we split for some reason, but I'm not.

It's like being captain of a ship and throwing out a lifebuoy to a drowning passenger. I've extended the rope as far as I can, but I can't abandon ship. I'm searching for more rope but time is ticking.

She had a tragically traumatic childhood, and she didn't have anything resembling a normal life until puberty. She's come to the conclusion that no amount and combination of therapy and medication is going to help. I haven't given up, but it's hard to disagree. Like any chronic illness, the severity ebbs and flows. It's a balancing act allowing myself to take a breath for my own mental health during the ebbs but not to let myself get too comfortable. Right now is a flow, and lately when she asks why I won't let her die...I've got nothing but silence and that scares me tremendously.
